questions.explain: Five stages: Reactive (50–65% over baseline — no tagging, no allocation, Multi-AZ everywhere, zero RI coverage), Aware (35–50% — spreadsheet, informal, waste visible but unowned), Structured (15–30% — enforced tagging, showback, monthly rightsizing, ≥60% RI coverage), Optimized (5–15% over minimum — >80% prod RI, scheduled start/stop, pooling, query attribution, gp3), Autonomous (within 5% — CI/CD guardrails, pre-bill anomaly detection, programmatic RI management, cost-per-transaction metric).
options: Reactive (50–65% over) → Aware (35–50%) → Structured (15–30%) → Optimized (5–15% over min) → Autonomous (within 5%) — each stage defined by observable practices like enforced tagging, RI coverage, and query-level attribution
questions.q: What are the five stages of the Database FinOps Maturity Model and their overspend bands?

questions.explain: A 200-instance RDS estate with no program spends roughly $2.4M annually on compute; the same workload through the maturity model lands near $960K — a $1.44M annual difference before storage, transfer, or licensing. The concrete levers: RI coverage (db.r6g.2xlarge: $8,409.60/yr on-demand vs $5,045.76 1-yr no-upfront = $3,363.84/instance/yr; 50 instances = $168,192/yr), gp2→gp3 ($23/mo per 1TB; $27,600/yr for 100), and dev/staging scheduling ($2,139/yr per m6g.xlarge; $64,170/yr for 30).
options: No-program $2.4M → mature $960K/yr ($1.44M gap), driven by RI coverage ($168k/yr per 50 instances), gp2→gp3 ($27.6k/yr per 100), and dev/staging scheduling ($64k/yr per 30)
questions.q: What is the financial scale of the maturity gap?

questions.explain: Stage 1→2 requires three foundations: mandatory tagging, cost allocation, and a baseline query (CUR/Athena, Cost Management, or BigQuery billing export) showing spend by resource. The goal at Stage 2 is not action but accountability — publish the numbers to engineering leads weekly; ownership follows visibility within two to four weeks.
options: At Stage 2: mandatory tagging, cost allocation, and baseline queries — the goal is accountability, not action; ownership follows visibility within 2–4 weeks
questions.q: What moves an organization from Reactive to Aware?

questions.explain: Four practices define Stage 4: query-level cost attribution (Query Store weighted_cost_score = CPU×0.40 + logical reads×0.35 + memory grant KB×0.25 guiding rightsizing), gp2→gp3 migration, environment scheduling (10h/weekday business hours), and connection pooling. These make savings granular, persistent, and embedded in daily operations.
options: Stage 4 is about buying bigger instances
Query-level cost attribution (weighted CPU/IO/memory score), gp2→gp3 migration, environment start/stop scheduling, and connection pooling
questions.q: What four practices define the Stage 3→4 transition to Optimized?

questions.explain: Stage 5 is sustained, not reached once: cost drift is detected and corrected automatically without a human noticing a bill. Three systems: anomaly detection with automatic remediation (CloudWatch leading indicators — CPU band, FreeStorageSpace, connections, IOPS, ReadLatency >20ms — checked every 15 minutes), RI lifecycle management with expiration tracking, and cost-per-transaction instrumentation embedded in application telemetry and reviewed in sprint retrospectives.
options: Stage 5 = anomaly detection with auto-remediation on CloudWatch leading indicators, programmatic RI lifecycle management, and cost-per-transaction in application telemetry reviewed in retrospectives — drift is corrected without human intervention
questions.q: What sustains Stage 5 Autonomous cost governance?
